who: Kell Freeman Mitchell, historian of US diplomacy and women, University of Memphis; PhD University of Georgia.

evidence.says: The departmental memorial identifies Kell Freeman Mitchell as a specialist in American diplomatic history with a Georgia PhD who taught at Memphis for almost half a century.
Mitchell joined the department in 1963, earned his MA and PhD at Georgia, and helped introduce women’s history in the early 1970s.
The similarly spelled Kel Mitchell authority is associated with Good Burger and Prank Day.
This Kelly Mitchell authority identifies the author of Gold Wars and describes work in strategic business analysis.

notes: Checked all eleven supplied LC records. Their names and cited works concern other people; none identifies Kell Freeman Mitchell.

who: George T. Morgan, Jr. (George Thomas Morgan), historian at the University of Houston.

evidence.says: Houston’s dissertation list names George Morgan, Jr. as adviser of Marta Sue Zulauf (1982) and James C. Maroney (1975), with the same titles as the supplied student records.
The authority cites The Woodlands (1987), naming George T. Morgan, Jr. and the Department of History, University of Houston; its heading expands the name to George Thomas Morgan.

notes: Exact matches to both students and the candidate’s departmental affiliation establish the identity.

who: D. Brendan Nagle, ancient historian at the University of Southern California; PhD USC 1968.

evidence.says: USC identifies Nagle as emeritus professor of history, records his USC PhD in 1968 and department chairmanship in 1976–1983, and lists The Ancient World and The Roman World.
The authority cites The Ancient World, identifying D. Brendan Nagle with USC’s Department of History, and also cites The Roman World.

notes: Same full name, institution, ancient-history works, and exact doctoral institution and year.

who: Joseph A. November, historian of science, medicine, and computing at the University of South Carolina; PhD Princeton 2006.

evidence.says: The history faculty profile identifies Joseph A. November, records his Princeton PhD, and describes research on biomedical computing.
The July 2006 SHOT newsletter reports that Joseph A. November would receive his Princeton PhD that summer and join South Carolina as assistant professor of history.
The authority identifies Joseph Adam November from the title page of Digitizing Life (2006), with supporting information from Princeton University Archives.
The program names Joseph November as director of Bethany Lynn Johnson’s history dissertation, In the Aftermath of the Lost Pandemic: Philadelphia, 1918–1923.

notes: The candidate’s dissertation, degree, appointment, and named student agree.

who: Harry P. Owens, Civil War historian at the University of Mississippi; doctorate Florida State University.

evidence.says: The university identifies Harry P. Owens as its history professor and Florida State doctorate recipient, and specifically identifies Christopher Losson as his MA and PhD student.
The Harry P. Owens authority cites Perspectives and Irony in American Slavery (1976).
The university’s history symposium record lists Perspectives and Irony in American Slavery, edited by Harry P. Owens, as a symposium publication.

notes: The named student, doctoral university, full name, and authority’s book agree.

who: Elizabeth (Liza) Piper, environmental historian at the University of Alberta; PhD York University 2005.

evidence.says: The history department lists doctoral supervision under Elizabeth Piper and graduate supervision under Liza Piper.
Liza Piper’s university profile identifies her as a professor of environmental history working on northern and western Canada.
The academic biography identifies Liza Piper as an Alberta history professor who completed her PhD at York University, studying subarctic industrial development.
The sole candidate, Elizabeth Spear Piper, is identified through Patterns of Violent Juvenile Recidivism (1983).
The government bibliography identifies Patterns of Violent Juvenile Recidivism as a 1983 doctoral dissertation at the University of Pennsylvania.

notes: The candidate is associated with a Pennsylvania doctorate on juvenile offending; the supervisor is the York-trained environmental historian Liza Piper.

who: Douglas R. Reynolds (Douglas Robertson Reynolds), historian of modern China and Japan at Georgia State University; doctoral training at Columbia.

evidence.says: The publisher’s description identifies Douglas R. Reynolds as professor of history at Georgia State, specializing in modern China and Japan, and author of China, 1898–1912: The Xinzheng Revolution and Japan.

The authority connects Douglas Robertson Reynolds with The Chinese Industrial Cooperative Movement and the Political Polarization of Wartime China, and records Douglas R. Reynolds and Ren Da as name forms for Xin Zheng Ge Ming Yu Riben.
Reynolds’s own account identifies him as professor of history at Georgia State and describes his training in Columbia’s Chinese and Japanese history program.

notes: Institution, specialization, expanded name, and linked Chinese-history works agree; the other supplied Reynolds authorities are different name forms or fields.

who: Kodi A. Roberts, historian at Louisiana State University; PhD history, University of Chicago 2012.

evidence.says: LSU’s faculty profile records Kodi Roberts’s Chicago history PhD in 2012 and lists Voodoo & Power: The Politics of Religion in New Orleans, 1889–1940 (2015).
The Kodi A. Roberts authority identifies him from Voodoo and Power (2015).
The LSU graduate student directory lists Kodi Roberts as an adviser in African American history.

notes: Exact doctoral institution and year, LSU affiliation, and the authority’s book establish the match.
